newsitem.title: HUNGARY: Central Europe will lead in rising demand for steel-stud.
newsitem.headline: Central Europe will lead in rising demand for steel-stud.

text.p: Steel consumption in Europe will grow to 188 to 200 million tonnes per year by 2000, with the fastest growth in central Europe, researchers said on Tuesday.
"Central Europe's consumption is likely to grow the fastest by 26 to 36 percent," Pal Tardy of Hungarian research company InnoFerCo Rt told a news conference.
He said the demand would grow from a level of 173 million tonnes in 1994 and noted that "excess (steel) production capacity remains the biggest problem in the region".

With narrowing export prospects outside Europe, capacity shortages are unlikely to occur, thus central and eastern Europe should concentrate on restructuring rather than capacity increase, the study said.
Steel consumption in the region is directly linked to macroeconomic figures, Tardy said.
"GDP growth, industrial output and steel consumption move in parallel," he said. "All three registered a downward trend until 1993, and are on a slow upward slope now."
He added that steel consumption in Russia and the Ukraine is still dropping but the rate of decrease is slowing down.

The study has formulated two scenarios, the more pessimistic forecasting a 16 million tonnes drop in Europe's steel production by the year 2000, with a more optimistic version prediciting a 10 million tonnes rise.
